rationale: StatementTyped.letValue types the value first and passes exactly its intermediate environment and resulting type to BindingTyped; the conclusion binds the same pattern/value pair. SequenceTyped.cons threads the statement output into the remaining sequence, while nil returns the same well-formed environment. The nil well-formedness premise is the earlier global environment convention rather than a new semantic hypothesis. ProgramTyped is exactly well-formed classes and an existential final environment for a sequence from the empty environment. Neither SequenceTyped nor ProgramTyped requires that final environment to be empty, so retained empty and initialized variables agree with the no-scope-exit prose. These definitions use Unpacking.Statement and the previously introduced binding patterns, rather than silently returning to the smaller single-variable language.
